conflicts.fact: Behaviour of the stool when the jerrycan is placed at the centre versus a corner, and which stool state is the 'stable' baseline
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: three-legged stool stays stable with a sufuria at the centre and topples with the jerrycan at the corner. Lesson 2: describes the jerrycan at the corner vs near the centre (centre gives small moment, stays upright), a different comparison from Lesson 1 (sufuria vs jerrycan). Lesson 6: the 4-legged wide stool with the load at the corner is 'close to the tipping threshold', whereas the anchoring phenomenon and Lessons 1 and 5 say it barely tilts and survives.
